## Bayesian Reporting Workflow

The Bayesian approach in ggstatsplot uses the `BayesFactor` package internally. The goal is to quantify *how much* evidence exists for or against an effect, rather than simply crossing a significance threshold.

### Setting priors

```{r}
#| fig-alt: "Violin and box plots of SysBP 6m against TreatmentGroup, with the test result in the subtitle, titled 'SBP at 6 months by treatment (Bayesian, default prior)'."
library(ggstatsplot)

# Default Cauchy prior (r = 0.707) — appropriate for most comparisons
ggbetweenstats(
  data         = bp,
  x            = TreatmentGroup,
  y            = SysBP_6m,
  type         = "bayes",
  bf.prior     = 0.707,        # scale of Cauchy prior on effect size
  title        = "SBP at 6 months by treatment (Bayesian, default prior)"
)

# Narrow prior — use if you expect a small effect
ggbetweenstats(
  data         = bp,
  x            = TreatmentGroup,
  y            = SysBP_6m,
  type         = "bayes",
  bf.prior     = 0.5,
  title        = "SBP at 6 months by treatment (narrow prior)"
)
```

With this much data the prior hardly matters: BF₁₀ is about 100,000 with r = 0.707 and about 94,000 with r = 0.5
(computed with `BayesFactor::ttestBF()`). The prior matters most when the evidence is weak; report which one you used.

### Reporting Bayes factors in text

For SBP **at 6 months** (control 135.7, intervention 125.1 mmHg):

> "A Bayesian independent-samples t-test (Cauchy prior, r = 0.707) gave extreme evidence for a difference in
> systolic BP at 6 months between the treatment groups, BF₁₀ ≈ 1 × 10⁵."

For SBP **at baseline**, where randomisation should leave no difference:

> "The Bayes factor favoured no baseline difference between the groups, BF₁₀ = 0.19 (BF₀₁ = 5.3, moderate
> evidence for the null)."

::: {.callout-tip}
## Key distinction: BF₁₀ vs BF₀₁
- **BF₁₀**: evidence for H₁ over H₀ (use when testing for an effect)
- **BF₀₁ = 1/BF₁₀**: evidence for H₀ over H₁ (use when supporting the null)

ggstatsplot prints **log<sub>e</sub>(BF₀₁)** in the subtitle; convert with BF₁₀ = exp(−value).
A p-value cannot show support for "no difference"; a Bayes factor can.
:::

## `grouped_*` Functions — Faceted Comparisons

The `grouped_*` variants run the same comparison separately within each level of a grouping variable and combine the results into a faceted plot.

```{r}
#| fig-alt: "Violin and box plots of SysBP 6m against SmokingStatus, with the test result in the subtitle, titled 'SBP at 6 months by smoking status, stratified by arm'."
# Compare SBP across smoking groups, separately in each treatment arm
grouped_ggbetweenstats(
  data             = bp,
  x                = SmokingStatus,
  y                = SysBP_6m,
  grouping.var     = TreatmentGroup,   # one panel per arm
  annotation.args  = list(title = "SBP at 6 months by smoking status, stratified by arm"),
  plotgrid.args    = list(ncol = 2)
)
```

```{r}
#| fig-alt: "Scatter plot of SysBP 0m against Age, with a regression line, marginal histograms and the correlation test, titled 'Age vs baseline SBP by treatment group'."
# Correlation stratified by TreatmentGroup group
grouped_ggscatterstats(
  data         = bp,
  x            = Age,
  y            = SysBP_0m,
  grouping.var = TreatmentGroup,
  annotation.args = list(title = "Age vs baseline SBP by treatment group")
)
```

**Available grouped functions:**

- `grouped_ggbetweenstats()`
- `grouped_ggwithinstats()`
- `grouped_ggscatterstats()`
- `grouped_gghistostats()`
- `grouped_ggbarstats()`
- `grouped_ggpiestats()`
- `grouped_ggcorrmat()`
- `grouped_ggdotplotstats()`

## `ggcorrmat()` — Correlation Matrix

Visualises pairwise correlations across multiple continuous variables with significance annotations.

```{r}
#| fig-alt: "Correlation matrix heat map, titled 'Correlation Matrix — Baseline Variables'."
ggcorrmat(
  data   = bp |> select(Age, SysBP_0m, SysBP_3m, SysBP_6m,
                                 BMI, Cholesterol),
  title  = "Correlation Matrix — Baseline Variables",
  type   = "parametric"     # "parametric", "nonparametric", "robust", "bayes"
)
```

**Choosing the correlation type:**

| `type` | Method | When to use |
|---|---|---|
| `"parametric"` | Pearson's r | Continuous, approximately normal |
| `"nonparametric"` | Spearman's ρ | Ordinal or skewed distributions |
| `"robust"` | Percentage bend r | Presence of outliers |
| `"bayes"` | Bayesian r | Quantify evidence, not just significance |

## Combining with patchwork

All ggstatsplot outputs are ggplot2 objects and compose naturally with `patchwork`.

```{r}
#| fig-alt: "Violin and box plots of SysBP 0m against TreatmentGroup, with the test result in the subtitle, titled 'Baseline SBP'."
library(patchwork)

p1 <- ggbetweenstats(
  data  = bp,
  x     = TreatmentGroup,
  y     = SysBP_0m,
  title = "Baseline SBP"
)

p2 <- ggbetweenstats(
  data  = bp,
  x     = TreatmentGroup,
  y     = SysBP_3m,
  title = "3-Month SBP"
)

p3 <- ggscatterstats(
  data  = bp,
  x     = SysBP_0m,
  y     = SysBP_3m,
  title = "Baseline vs 3-Month SBP"
)

# Compose: two plots on top, one full-width below
(p1 | p2) / p3 +
  plot_annotation(
    title   = "Blood pressure outcomes by treatment group",
    caption = "Source: simulated BP trial (data/README.md)"
  )
```

## Publication-ready output

```{r}
#| fig-alt: "Violin and box plots of SysBP 6m against TreatmentGroup, with the test result in the subtitle, titled 'Systolic blood pressure at 6 months by treatment group'."
library(ggplot2)

pub_plot <- ggbetweenstats(
  data             = bp,
  x                = TreatmentGroup,
  y                = SysBP_6m,
  type             = "parametric",
  pairwise.display = "significant",    # show only significant comparisons
  p.adjust.method  = "bonferroni",
  title            = "Systolic blood pressure at 6 months by treatment group",
  xlab             = "Treatment group",
  ylab             = "Systolic BP (mmHg)",
  package          = "RColorBrewer",
  palette          = "Set1"
) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    plot.title       = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
    axis.line        = element_line(linewidth = 0.5),
    plot.caption     = element_text(hjust = 0, colour = "grey50")
  ) +
  labs(caption = "Bonferroni-adjusted pairwise comparisons shown for p < 0.05")

# Save at print quality
ggsave(file.path(tempdir(), "sbp_by_treatment.png"),   # in a project: "figures/..."
       pub_plot, width = 8, height = 6, dpi = 300)
```

## Case Study: Healthcare Data

A complete example on the simulated BP trial: the change in SBP from baseline to 6 months across treatment groups, overall and by smoking status.

```{r}
#| fig-alt: "Violin and box plots of sbp change against TreatmentGroup, with the test result in the subtitle, titled 'Change in SBP at 6 months'."
library(ggstatsplot)
library(dplyr)
library(patchwork)

# Derive SBP change variable
study_data <- bp |>
  mutate(sbp_change = SysBP_6m - SysBP_0m)

# 1. Overall change by TreatmentGroup
p_overall <- ggbetweenstats(
  data  = study_data,
  x     = TreatmentGroup,
  y     = sbp_change,
  type  = "parametric",
  title = "Change in SBP at 6 months"
)

# 2. Stratified by tobacco type
p_strat <- grouped_ggbetweenstats(
  data         = study_data,
  x            = TreatmentGroup,
  y            = sbp_change,
  grouping.var = SmokingStatus,
  annotation.args = list(title = "SBP change stratified by smoking status"),
  plotgrid.args = list(ncol = 3)
)

# View each
p_overall
p_strat
```

## Quick reference

```{r}
#| eval: false
# Bayesian comparison
ggbetweenstats(data = df, x = group, y = outcome, type = "bayes",
               bf.prior = 0.707)

# Faceted comparisons
grouped_ggbetweenstats(data = df, x = group, y = outcome,
                       grouping.var = stratifier)

# Correlation matrix
ggcorrmat(data = df |> select(var1, var2, var3, var4))

# Compose with patchwork
(p1 | p2) / p3 + plot_annotation(title = "Figure 1")
```
